title: Coordinate Laplacian moment bound
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, suppose $f\colon \Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ takes only the values $-1$ and $1$, and choose a coordinate $i$ and an exponent $p$ with $1\le p\le 2$. The product expectation of the $p$th power of the absolute value of the coordinate Laplacian of $f$ is at most the influence of $f$ at coordinate $i$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$B$ is a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ containing the constant-one function
